title: Define capture and replay host API
description:
Define the core host-facing capture and replay API after HostSession exists. The flake/devshell work now gives us reproducible validation, and HostSession gives us a concrete sync facade. This issue should focus on a minimal, transport-independent capture stream for replaying HostSession inputs and comparing semantic outputs without BLE/runtime dependencies.

Scope: stable owned capture records for link up/down, notification bytes, ticks, and host commands; a replay helper that drives HostSession from those records; and tests proving whole-notification, one-byte, and arbitrary-chunk notification replay can produce equivalent semantic events for fake sessions.

Out of scope: advertisement/GATT inventory, user annotations, redaction metadata, on-disk PEVCAP/JSONL schema, BLE adapter collection, and concrete device captures.
design: Keep implementation in cutout-core as owned value types: CaptureRecord and CaptureReplaySummary or equivalent. Notification records own Vec<u8>; replay borrows only for the immediate HostSession call. Reuse HostSession::drain_outputs for semantic comparison. Provide small helper functions for replaying records and extracting events; avoid serde and file IO in this core slice. If capture metadata or file schema is needed, create child issues under capture/CLI rather than expanding this type layer.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for owned notification capture records, replay driving HostSession without BLE/runtime types, whole-notification versus one-byte replay equivalence, arbitrary-chunk replay equivalence, command/tick/link record replay, and output ordering preservation.
Capture/replay core types use stable explicit fields and owned payloads; no serde, file IO, async runtime, BLE, platform, or source-scanning tests are introduced.
Any larger advertisement/GATT inventory, annotation/redaction, on-disk schema, or capture CLI work discovered is added as beads issues.
Validation uses nix develop and includes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and cargo deny check. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.
notes: Implementation standard: follow Rust TDD red/green/refactor. Knowledge from HostSession: replay should drive the same facade methods hosts will use, and snapshots/diagnostics should be derived from emitted events rather than capture-specific hidden state. Keep this deterministic and low-allocation where practical.

Implement REALTIME_DATA command ID 31, including state, footpad state, stop condition, alerts, timestamps, and dynamically described telemetry values.

Acceptance: normalized events include both canonical fields and namespaced Refloat extension values.
notes: Implementation standard: start from a failing test and keep the work TDD-first. Use property tests for parsers and state machines, mutation tests where they add signal, and prefer functional, bounded, low-allocation code where it does not materially slow implementation. Keep the protocol engine synchronous and transport-independent; Tokio/smol/mio stay in adapter crates only. Once a device or protocol is fully specced, verify it against actual Bluetooth hardware before closing the issue.

title: Plan concrete UniFFI session object boundary
description: Plan the concrete non-generic session object boundary for UniFFI after the core HostSession facade shape is proven. The core facade can be generic over ProtocolSession for Rust tests, but Swift/Kotlin need concrete constructors, DTOs, owned buffers, and error/result shapes.\n\nAcceptance: proposed UniFFI API has no Rust generics, borrowed buffers, trait objects, async streams, or platform transport types crossing the boundary; it maps HostSession inputs/outputs/snapshots/diagnostics into stable Swift/Kotlin-friendly DTOs; tests or generated binding smoke checks are identified before implementation.
